definition: A hypothetical artificial general intelligence that can apply its own intelligence to improving its design, so each round of self-improvement yields a more capable successor.
details: In 1965, Good argued that an “ultraintelligent machine” able to surpass human intellect could design still better machines, triggering a self-amplifying loop often called the intelligence explosion. Recursive general intelligence names that loop explicitly: general problem-solving ability plus the capacity to modify the very system doing the solving. The idea underpins debates about superintelligence and how quickly capabilities might compound.

citation.title: Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine
